question: The lengths of a pair of parallel sides of a trapezium are 20 cm and 25 cm, respectively, and the perpendicular distance between these two sides is 14 cm. What is the area (in cm² ) of the trapezium?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of Trapezium = Average of parallel sides × Height

Area = [(20 + 25) ÷ 2] × 14

Area = 45 × 7

Area = 315 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 315 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths of parallel sides (a and b) = 20 cm and 25 cm

Perpendicular distance between parallel sides (h) = 14 cm

 

 
•

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × (Perpendicular distance)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (20 + 25) × 14

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 45 × 14

⇒ Area = 45 × 7

⇒ Area = 315

**∴ The correct answer is 315 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Parallelogram

The area of a parallelogram is the product of its base and corresponding height. Formula: Area = base × height.

Area of a Rhombus

The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonal lengths. Formula: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides is called the median. Length of median = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides).

Area of a Triangle

The area is half the product of its base and perpendicular height. Formula: Area = 1/2 × base × height.
